why_this_grade: Ordinary: GAAP margin on sales. Banks: net interest margin after provisions is the analogue, not GAAP net margin on 'revenue'. REITs: GAAP margin polluted by depreciation; FFO margin is the parallel.
settling_evidence_needed: Bank 10-K NII/provision breakout; REIT FFO reconciliation

why_this_grade: Ordinary: cash after capex. Banks: 'capex' meaningless; OCF-to-holders differs. REITs: needs AFFO (capex incl. maintenance) not raw FCF.
settling_evidence_needed: AFFO disclosure; bank operating-cash-flow definition memo

why_this_grade: Ordinary: earnings quality. Banks/REITs: denominator (NI) itself model-mismatched, ratio inherits the mismatch.
Accrual amazon: working-capital accruals differ by model; loan-loss provisions (banks) and straight-line rent/depreciation (REITs) dominate. Needs per-model calibration.
Ordinary: demand growth. Banks: NII + noninterest split required. REITs: same-store NOI / FFO growth, not GAAP revenue.
Same denominator problem as margins; REIT EPS is structurally the wrong object (use FFO/share path).
Ordinary: cash engine. Banks: OCF definition differs. REITs: AFFO growth analogue.
Ordinary: leverage. Banks: deposits ARE the business — leverage ratio inverted in meaning. REITs: Debt/EBITDA used, but EBITDA ≠ FFO; NetDebt/EBITDAre is the native gauge.
Ordinary: debt service. Banks: interest expense is COGS-like; coverage inverted. REITs: fixed-charge coverage analogue exists but differs.
settling_evidence_needed: Bank NII framing; REIT fixed-charge coverage

why_this_grade: Ordinary: liquidity. Banks/REITs: balance-sheet structure makes current/non-current split meaningless (maturity transformation; property held long).
Share-count mechanics are model-free (ATM issuance, buybacks). Keep everywhere.
P/S,P/E percentiles need model-native multiples (P/TBV banks; P/FFO,AFFO yield REITs). Current percentiles benchmark the wrong ratio.
Ordinary: channel stuffing signal. Banks: 'receivables' are loans — different object. REITs: rents receivable, small/thin.
